$note: Single source for every number in spec §5.6 (R5.7). Generated by measuring commit 3176725 (main, tip of Wave 2 — 'docs: Wave 2 gate browser flows recorded') with scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs's own method, then hand-tightened. Fix round on 2026-09-07 (Opus review of c6fef80) re-measured the full built tree — not just the spec's 12 anticipated routes — and found four more app routes the original generation never looked at: /preview, /login, /admin and / (`scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs`'s own reverse check now fails the gate if a fifth ever slips in unnoticed). Do not hand-write a number here without re-running the measurement; the whole point of this gate is that it reflects a real build, not the spec's provisional table.
method: docs/research/v2/codebase-audit.md §3: read each route's .next/server/app/**/page_client-reference-manifest.js, resolve its entryJSFiles list against on-disk .next/static/chunks/*.js sizes, sum uncompressed bytes.
rules: (a) no route's budgetBytes may exceed its v1Bytes, ever, even when the measured tree is currently over budget. scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs enforces this at load time — a budgetBytes above v1Bytes fails the gate before a single route is measured.

(b) every route whose measured size exceeds specTargetBytes (the spec §5.6 direction) carries a named row in `ledger` saying which library is responsible and whether it is split, deferred, or accepted. Enforced: each ledger row now carries a `routes` array, and the gate fails if a route measures over its specTargetBytes without appearing in at least one row's `routes`.

(c) every route the build actually produces must appear either in `routes` (with a real budget) or in `unbudgetedRoutes` (with a stated reason) — scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs diffs the measured tree against both and fails the gate on anything in neither, so a route cannot go silently ungated.

ledger.note: This is not one of the spec's anticipated overages — it is a real bug found by this measurement, present identically on all 13 routes above, including /preview (fix-round finding: /preview renders the same shell and buddy widget as every authenticated route, and its manifest carries the identical 475,150-byte leak chunk `415yhzio7b-ph.js`, confirmed by direct chunk inspection on 2026-09-07). Before the fix, one 475,150-byte chunk carries the leak (confirmed by content: it has zod's `ZodObject`/`ZodString` exports and the literal string "deepseek"); state.ts wants only the REFUSAL string constant, but a non-type-only import of one export from an agent module pulls the whole module — zod included — into every route that renders the buddy widget in the shell (today, every authenticated route plus /preview). Verified directly: patching state.ts in a disposable worktree to hold its own copy of the REFUSAL string instead of importing it, then rebuilding, drops every one of these routes by exactly 375,465 bytes (confirmed identical across all 13 routes) — Turbopack re-packs the remaining ~99,685 bytes of that chunk (the buddy widget's own legitimate code) into a smaller, separate chunk rather than deleting it outright, so 375,465 bytes — not the full 475,150-byte chunk — is the true, fixable cost. Fix: move REFUSAL into a client-safe module with no zod import (or re-export it from a `'use client'`-safe barrel that never imports the agent files), not read from src/lib/agents/buddy.ts on the client. Out of T3.1's ownership (src/components/buddy/** belongs to T2.11) — reported and verified rather than fixed here, and still unfixed as of this fix round (2026-09-07: `src/components/buddy/state.ts:4` still reads `import { REFUSAL } from '@/lib/agents/buddy'`). Every budgetBytes value above already excludes this 375,465 bytes (i.e. assumes the fix lands), so perf:bundle fails on the current tree until it does; that failure is the gate correctly biting on a genuine, newly measured regression, not a bug in this script. W4FIX-B2 (2026-09-07): fixed. `src/components/buddy/state.ts` no longer imports `REFUSAL` from `@/lib/agents/buddy` at all — it holds its own byte-for-byte duplicate of the frozen string (pinned against the real agent-module export by `state.test.ts`'s own equality assertion, and guarded against regressing back to an import by `src/components/buddy/no-zod-in-client.test.ts`, a source scan proven to fail against a planted `import { REFUSAL as X } from '@/lib/agents/buddy'`). A single `requestAnimationFrame` defer (the fix round's first attempt) was still not enough -- confirmed live it still fetched all three chunks under `reduced` -- because `requestAnimationFrame` runs before the browser paints, while the `useSyncExternalStore` correction fires from a passive effect that only runs after that paint; one rAF still lands before it. `src/components/motion/Reveal.tsx`'s effect now defers the load by two `requestAnimationFrame`s (a `raf`, and a `raf2` scheduled from inside it), both cancelled in the cleanup -- re-measured live three times in a row against this scratch build: `reducedMotion: 'reduce'` on `/login` now requests zero gsap chunks (`NONE`), while `reducedMotion: 'no-preference'` still requests all three and the split still runs (`childCount: 1`, nested `SplitText` mask divs present). No byte moved -- `node scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs` on this build reports byte-identical totals to the pre-fix-round build (e.g. `/` 93.6 KB, `/admin` 262.8 KB, `/login` 427.6 KB) -- this is a load-timing correction only, not a payload change, so `bytes: 0`.
